channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Freedom Holding Corp. Expands Global Ecosystem Beyond Kazakhstan, Faces Russian Prosecutor General's Lawsuit
item.description: Freedom Holding Corp., primarily operating in Kazakhstan, is expanding its business into Europe, the US, and Asia, recently acquiring a Turkish bank and reporting a 40% revenue increase. Concurrently, Russia's Prosecutor General's Office has filed a lawsuit against the group. The holding company, registered in Nevada and traded on Nasdaq, operates in 24 countries with 264 offices.

item.title: Piskent District Head Reprimanded for Insulting Farmers
item.description: The head of Piskent district, Muzaffar Aripov, received a reprimand for violating ethical conduct and professional ethics. This action followed the spread of an audio recording where he allegedly insulted farmers and threatened to confiscate their land. The district administration acknowledged inappropriate communication.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reduces Oil Production but Increases Fuel Output
item.description: Kazakhstan's oil production decreased by 8.3% to 69.4 million tons in January-September, while fuel production rose by 2.4% to 11.9 million tons. Negotiations are underway with major subsoil users to increase oil extraction volumes. The forecast for 2026 oil production is 96 million tons.

item.title: King and Queen of Belgium to visit Almaty; traffic restrictions possible
item.description: The King and Queen of Belgium are scheduled to visit Almaty on October 14, potentially leading to temporary traffic restrictions in certain areas. The visit includes events with Kazakh and Belgian officials, as well as business and academic representatives. The royal couple arrived in Astana on October 11.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Tax Reform Generates 3 Trillion Tenge, VAT Leading Revenue Source
item.description: Kazakhstan's tax reform has injected an additional 3 trillion tenge into the economy, with Value Added Tax (VAT) being the primary contributor. Minister of National Economy Serik Zhumangarin stated that the reform is currently the sole source of cash for the economy. Despite a VAT rate increase to 16%, the collection plan was met at 90%, resulting in a shortfall of nearly 700 billion tenge.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Rejects European Proposals for Migrant Resettlement
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has rejected proposals from several European countries to accept migrants from Afghanistan and African nations, according to Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev. In exchange, these countries offered employment opportunities for skilled Kyrgyz workers. Bishkek stated it would not negotiate on these terms. The minister did not specify the countries or the number of migrants involved.

item.title: Kazakhstan Stores to Prioritize Domestic Goods Starting October 20
item.description: Starting October 20, stores across Kazakhstan will be required to allocate more shelf space to domestic products. This measure aims to promote local manufacturers' goods. Seventy-two memorandums have been signed with retail chains for this purpose, though specific allocation quotas per product category are not yet defined. Total trade volume reached 61 trillion tenge in the first nine months of 2026.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Settle Debts of 108 Hospitals and Clinics by Year-End
item.description: Kazakhstan aims to resolve the financial issues of 108 hospitals and clinics with overdue debts by the end of the year, according to Finance Minister Madi Takiev. Significant work has been done in the mandatory social health insurance system, updating information systems and centralizing payments. The ministry expects these clinics to be out of deficit by the first quarter of 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Continue Annual Pension Indexation Based on Inflation, Assures Official
item.description: Kazakhstan's pension payments will continue to be indexed annually to the official inflation rate, confirmed Vice Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin. He stated that pensions are raised in accordance with inflation levels, and there are no plans for changes. The base for indexation is the inflation rate; if it's higher, the indexation will be higher.

item.title: Four New Sections Added to Kazakhstan's Average Speed Control System on Toll Roads
item.description: Kazakhstan has activated average speed control systems on four additional sections of its toll roads, bringing the total to 15. The new routes include sections connecting Oral to the Russian border (Samara), Aktobe to the Russian border (Orenburg), Kostanay to Denisovka, and Kandyagash to Makat. The system measures average speed between control arches.

item.title: Kazakh Minister Reports Success of Tax Reform, VAT Leads Budget Revenue
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of National Economy, Serik Zhumangarin, stated that the tax reform has been highly successful, with VAT becoming the leading source of budget revenue. Despite economic challenges, the reform is projected to contribute at least 3.6 trillion tenge to the economy by year-end. The number of VAT-paying legal entities has significantly increased.

item.title: C5+1 Diplomacy Raises Questions About Central Asia's Evolving Boundaries
item.description: The C5+1 format involving the United States prompts discussion on the definition of Central Asia. While politically it refers to five post-Soviet states, historical and strategic perspectives suggest a broader region potentially including Afghanistan, Iran, western China, and Mongolia. Early C5+1 discussions considered including Afghanistan, highlighting differing regional understandings.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Finance Minister Details Changes After Medical Insurance Fund Transfer
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of Finance, Madi Takiev, outlined changes following the transfer of the Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF) to the Ministry of Finance. A new information system, 'Kalkan,' now processes all payments. The primary goals are to reduce patient waiting times and eliminate out-of-pocket payments for services. The ministry has also worked on clearing debts owed by medical organizations.

item.title: Kazakhstan schedules early elections for maslikhat deputies on November 29
item.description: Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission has announced that early elections for maslikhat deputies at all levels will be held on November 29, 2026. This follows President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's decree on October 12 to prematurely terminate the powers of all maslikhats.

item.title: Uzbek doctor saves passenger's life on Tashkent-Seoul flight
item.description: An Uzbek doctor, Hasan Kamilov, saved a female passenger's life on an Uzbekistan Airways flight from Tashkent to Seoul. The passenger's condition rapidly deteriorated, with no detectable blood pressure or pulse. Dr. Kamilov administered emergency aid using his personal medication and onboard supplies, allowing the flight to continue.

item.title: Kazakhstan reports nearly 6 million tons of oil production losses amid CPC and Tengiz issues
item.description: Kazakhstan experienced oil production losses of up to 5.9 million tons, though some volumes were recovered. The Ministry of Energy stated that planned maintenance was postponed at Kashagan and Tengiz fields to compensate. Negotiations are underway to increase production. Losses have been reduced to 1.9 million tons.

item.title: Inflation in Kazakhstan slows to 9.3 percent
item.description: The government and National Bank of Kazakhstan have implemented measures to reduce inflation. Annual inflation slowed from 9.8% in August to 9.3% by the end of September, according to Egemen.kz. The slowdown is attributed to a decrease in the pace of food price increases, with food prices falling 0.1% in September.

item.title: Oil production declines at major fields in Kazakhstan: What's next?
item.description: Oil production has decreased at major fields in Kazakhstan. The article questions the future course of action for the country in response to this decline. Further details on the specific fields affected and the government's strategy are expected.

item.title: Former Afghan diplomat Aziz Boriz lauds launch of Asia-Plus Persian service
item.description: Aziz Boriz, a former Afghan diplomat and head of a UK-based research center, has praised the launch of the Persian service by Asia-Plus news agency. He described it as a strategic move that will aid in the unity and recognition of Farsi speakers worldwide regarding Tajikistan.

item.title: Former Helmand military official's body found six months after Taliban arrest
item.description: Taliban sources in Helmand report that the body of a former local police commander, Allahdad Badizi, has been returned to his family. He was arrested by Taliban intelligence six months prior, despite initial denials of his detention. He was reportedly tortured in prison.

item.title: Afghanistan and Iran discuss expanding industrial and mining cooperation
item.description: Iran's ambassador to Kabul met with officials from the Afghanistan Chamber of Industries and Mines to explore enhancing economic ties, joint investments, and strengthening collaboration in the industrial and mining sectors. The Afghan deputy for industry highlighted existing opportunities for cooperation.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Dissolves Local Councils, Calls for Snap Elections
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev dissolved local representative assemblies, known as maslikhats, by decree on October 12. Snap elections are mandated by December 12. This action follows the merger of the Amanat party into the pro-presidential Adilet party, raising questions about the legitimacy of incumbent deputies elected under the former party's banner.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission Sets November 29 for Maslikhat Elections
item.description: The Central Election Commission of Kazakhstan has scheduled elections for maslikhats at all levels for November 29. This announcement follows President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's decree on October 12 to prematurely terminate the powers of the maslikhats, requiring new elections within two months.

item.title: Kazakhstan Schedules Maslikhat Elections for Late November Following Presidential Decree
item.description: Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission has scheduled early elections for maslikhat deputies for November 29, following President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's October 12 decree to prematurely end the powers of all maslikhats. The election campaign will run for 48 days, with candidate nominations starting October 14.

item.title: Early Maslikhat Elections in Kazakhstan Set for November 29, Totaling 3,447 Mandates
item.description: Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission has scheduled early elections for maslikhats at all levels for November 29. A total of 3,447 mandates across 228 maslikhats will be contested. Candidate nominations begin October 14, with registration closing November 1, and campaigning ending November 28.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sets November 29 for Elections of Maslikhat Deputies
item.description: Kazakhstan has scheduled elections for maslikhat (local representative body) deputies for November 29. The Central Election Commission announced the start of the election campaign organization. Candidate nominations will run from October 14 to 27, with registration closing on November 1. The election results are expected by December 3.

item.title: Dushanbe Hosts Discussions on Attracting Investment for Agricultural Development
item.description: On October 12, 2026, Tajikistan's Minister of Agriculture met with development partners in Dushanbe to discuss attracting investment, implementing joint projects, and adopting international best practices in agriculture. Discussions focused on ensuring domestic food supply, increasing production, and expanding exports of organic produce.

item.title: Livestock Farming Expands in Uzbekistan's Jizzakh Region
item.description: Livestock farming is actively developing in the Arnasay district of Jizzakh region, Uzbekistan. A new breeding complex is under construction. The number of pedigree cattle has increased significantly, supported by improved fodder production and veterinary services, indicating growing agricultural initiatives.

item.title: Taliban Report 681 Afghan Migrants Returned in One Day
item.description: The Taliban announced that 681 Afghan migrants, comprising 156 families, returned to Afghanistan on a single day. Returns occurred through multiple border crossings, including Torkham, Spin Boldak, Silk Bridge, and Islam Qala, with the largest group entering via Nimroz province.

item.title: Natural Disasters in Afghanistan Claim 679 Lives in Past Year, Injuring Over 1,600
item.description: Afghanistan's Taliban-controlled disaster management authority reported that natural disasters in the past year resulted in 679 deaths and 1,643 injuries. The agency also stated that 4,470 homes were completely destroyed and 11,664 were damaged. Additionally, agricultural products from 77,874 acres and 10,438 gardens were lost.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host Film Days of Iran, Russia, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Dushanbe will host the third National Film Award 'Toji Somon' from October 15-20, 2026, featuring Film Days of Iran, Russia, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan. The event aims to showcase national cinematographic schools and foster cultural ties. Around 100 films are submitted for the competition.

item.title: Afghanistan Reports 36 Polio Cases This Year, Highest Globally
item.description: The World Health Organization confirmed a new polio case in Nangarhar province, bringing Afghanistan's total to 36 this year. An environmental polio case was also detected in Helmand. Afghanistan has the world's highest polio infection rate, with cases increasing from 21 in 2025. Pakistan is second, with six cases this year.

item.title: Uzbek Youth Crowned World Champions in Robotics
item.description: Young Uzbeks have become world champions in robotics. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev awarded the team's head coach the "Sodiq xizmatlari uchun" medal and team members the "Kelajak bunyodkori" medal for their achievement.

item.title: Tajikistan's Withdrawal from ICC: Gains and Losses Explored
item.description: Tajikistan's decision to withdraw from the International Criminal Court (ICC) is examined for its potential gains and losses. Dilrabo Samadova suggests the move does not absolve Tajikistan of past obligations. The article delves into the implications of this withdrawal.

item.title: Afghanistan Seeks International Aid for Climate Change and Disaster Mitigation
item.description: Afghanistan's Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, Mullah Abdul Ghani Baradar, called for fair international financial and technical assistance to combat climate change. He highlighted that Afghanistan suffers severe consequences from climate change despite minimal contribution to greenhouse gas emissions. Baradar urged against political interference in climate action and stressed shared responsibility for global climate protection.

item.title: Tajikistan Ratifies UN Convention Against Cybercrime to Enhance International Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan's parliament has ratified the UN Convention against Cybercrime, enabling law enforcement agencies to cooperate with other countries in combating cybercrimes and exchanging electronic evidence. This ratification aims to strengthen efforts against transnational cyber threats, which have been increasing in the country.

item.title: IAEA Mission in Astana to Prepare for Nuclear Power Plant Infrastructure Assessment
item.description: An IAEA mission is in Astana from October 12-15 to assist Kazakhstan in preparing for a comprehensive assessment of its nuclear power plant construction infrastructure. Experts are discussing a national self-assessment report and defining next steps before the main Integrated Nuclear Infrastructure Review (INIR) mission. Kazakhstan plans to build several nuclear power plants, with the first, "Balkhash," to be located near Ulken village in Almaty region.

item.title: Saneg Company's Oil Field Licenses in Uzbekistan Canceled Due to Non-Compliance
item.description: Licenses previously granted to Saneg company for oil field operations in Uzbekistan have been revoked due to failure to meet contractual obligations. The Director of the State Assets Management Agency (DABA) stated that the fields themselves were not privatized, but the right to use the subsoil was licensed. The licensing procedure for hydrocarbon exploration has since shifted to an auction-based system.

item.title: Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region's GDP Reaches 1.5 Billion Somoni in Nine Months
item.description: The Gross Regional Product (GRP) of the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO) reached 1 billion 509 million somoni in the first nine months of 2026, with an actual growth rate of 8%. Exports increased by 11.6% and paid services rose by 21.3% compared to the same period in 2025. Industrial production saw a 21.3% growth, and 40 new production facilities were launched, creating 153 jobs.

item.title: UNHCR Chief Urges Increased Support for Afghan Returnees and Protection of Girls' Rights
item.description: The UN High Commissioner for Refugees called for greater international investment to aid Afghan returnees, highlighting that millions are returning under difficult conditions, facing poverty, limited services, and restrictions on women and girls. The appeal was made during the 77th session of UNHCR’s Executive Committee.
